items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: You know my brother raced cars at Bonneville Salt Flats. He built the cars.

ctx.x: Do you know what I was doing when you came on? I was doing this, which is what I did last night. I played a Baroque Trumpet Recital, a 19th century recital. And I don’t play this a lot, you know. So I was playing mostly the low parts and they were playing the moving parts. Now I said, “You know I should really learn to play this more,” because I was playing the cornet solos at the end too. There were four of us. So we played baroque trumpet pieces for four baroque trumpets. I said, “Look, I can’t play the real…

You cannot practice music without practicing technique. You cannot practice technique without practicing music. See because I was doing like a lip slur exercise, you know they call them lip slurs, they’re really tongue slurs. But I was thinking about what it’s supposed to sound like to the audience. See? But at the same time when I’m practicing I’m finally tuning my engine. You know my brother raced cars at Bonneville Salt Flats. He built the cars. And you know he’d go out there every year and he’d come back and…
that, I said, “And eventually the mechanical part is behind you always, it’s more passive in the presentation. So I said, “When I play, even if it’s an etude,” I said, “what’s the use of practicing—
